Anticonvulsant Mood Stabilizers

valproate · lamotrigine · carbamazepine · oxcarbazepine · topiramateWhich adverse effect, and what do you check?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Drug script
Bottom line
  • Any rash on lamotrigine: stop it. After a lapse, restart at the starting dose; with valproate added, a lower dose and a slower titration
  • Valproate: level, liver tests and CBC before and during; confusion: ammonia; epigastric pain: lipase, and stop it for pancreatitis; neural tube defects
  • Carbamazepine: human leukocyte antigen (HLA) B*1502 before the first dose in Asian ancestry; CBC and sodium; an enzyme inducer, so oral contraceptives fail
What it is

Anticonvulsants used as mood stabilizers: valproate, carbamazepine and lamotrigine

Used for

Valproate: acute mania and maintenance; also seizures and migraine prevention

Carbamazepine: acute mania; also seizures and trigeminal neuralgia

Lamotrigine: maintenance and bipolar depression, not acute mania

Oxcarbazepine: as effective as carbamazepine for mood, better tolerated, less rash and liver toxicity

Topiramate: no proven benefit in bipolar disorder; migraine prevention; binge eating disorder

Which mood stabilizer, and which in pregnancy

Mechanism

Valproate, carbamazepine, lamotrigine: voltage-gated sodium channels blocked less neuronal firing

Valproate: gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transaminase blocked more GABA

Carbamazepine: liver enzymes induced, its own metabolism included

Fetal risk

Valproate: neural tube defects, cleft lip or palate, heart and urogenital defects; later cognitive deficits, autism, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder

Carbamazepine: neural tube defects, heart and craniofacial defects

Lamotrigine: relatively safe; first-trimester use may slightly raise the cleft lip or palate risk

Insights

Valproate makes lamotrigine riskier: it blocks lamotrigine clearance, so the level and the rash risk climb together

Valproate encephalopathy is a urea cycle problem: propionic acid, a valproate metabolite, blocks ammonia elimination, so a urea cycle disorder rules valproate out

Common effects at usual doses, by drugtap to open
ValproateNausea, vomiting, diarrhea; sedation, tremor, ataxia; weight gain; hair loss in 5% to 10%Hyperandrogenism in women; may raise the polycystic ovary syndrome risk
CarbamazepineSomnolence, nausea, diarrhea, rash; double vision, ataxiaVitamin D deficiency may occur, through enzyme induction
OxcarbazepineFatigue, dizziness, somnolence, double vision; hyponatremia
LamotrigineNausea, dizziness, fatigue, insomniaA benign rash in up to 10%, typically within the first 2 months
TopiramateSedation, cognitive slowing, speech trouble, weight loss, kidney stonesMay cause myopia and acute angle-closure glaucoma; metabolic acidosis
2Urgent risks
LamotrigineA new rash, mild or not, most often in the first 2 months; a benign rash and early Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) look alike

If any rash appears on lamotrigine, choose stopping the drug and substituting another agent.

Carbamazepine or lamotrigineA polymorphic rash with organ involvement, such as the liver, typically 2 to 8 weeks in: drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)

If DRESS appears, choose stopping the drug.

ValproateEpigastric pain with vomiting, at any dose and after any length of use

If it is acute pancreatitis, choose stopping the drug.

ValproateLethargy or confusion

If a patient on valproate becomes confused, choose a plasma ammonia level.

CarbamazepineAgranulocytosis or aplastic anemia, usually in the first 3 to 4 months

If a blood dyscrasia appears, choose stopping the drug; some reverse once it stops.

Carbamazepine overdoseDrowsiness, anticholinergic signs (high temperature, flushed skin, big pupils), fast pulse, low blood pressure

If the QRS widens or a dysrhythmia appears, choose sodium bicarbonate, with cardiac monitoring.

3Differential
Which drug, which effect, most tempting first
FindingDrugDecides it

A rash, typically with liver or other organ involvementDRESS: carbamazepine or lamotrigineTypically 2 to 8 weeks after the start
Agranulocytosis or aplastic anemia CarbamazepineFirst 3 to 4 months; some reverse once it stops
Low sodiumCarbamazepine or oxcarbazepine: syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH)Dose-dependent with carbamazepine
Confusion with a high ammoniaValproateUrea cycle blocked by a metabolite
Epigastric pain, vomitingValproate pancreatitisIdiosyncratic: not tied to dose or duration
Raised liver enzymesValproate; carbamazepine alsoValproate: first 6 months, mostly
Low plateletsValproateRare; a CBC before and during catches it
Weight loss, kidney stones, slowed thinkingTopiramateMay also cause myopia and acute angle-closure glaucoma
4Workup
Pause point
Years on a mood stabilizer, light drinking, then epigastric pain with vomiting Offered as alcohol or ibuprofen Valproate pancreatitis is idiosyncratic, so years on a steady dose do not rule it out; under 14 drinks a week and ibuprofen do not explain it → Valproate
A mild rash a few weeks into lamotrigine; the patient feels well Offered as a benign rash, so continue or a lower dose A benign rash and early SJS cannot be told apart, so any rash stops it → Stop the drug; substitute another agent

Neither answer depends on the dose or on how long the drug has been taken.

7Treatment
1

Any rashOn lamotrigine, mild or not

Stop lamotrigine; substitute another agent
2

RestartAfter lamotrigine stopped suddenly

Begin again at the starting dose and titrate up
3

Valproate addedTo lamotrigine

Lower the lamotrigine dose and titrate it more slowly
4

Serious reactionDRESS, valproate pancreatitis, a carbamazepine blood dyscrasia

Stop the drug

Pancreatitis resolves in most cases; some dyscrasias reverse

5

Carbamazepine overdoseAny severity

Supportive care: airway protection, IV fluids

QRS widening or a dysrhythmia: sodium bicarbonate

6

Pregnancy plannedOn valproate

If valproate continues: folic acid 4 mg daily

Whether to switch, and to what:

8Follow-up
Monitoring, by drug
WhenCheckWhy
Valproate, before and duringLevel (50 to 125 mcg/mL), liver tests, CBCToxicity; liver injury, mostly in the first 6 months; thrombocytopenia
Valproate, when indicatedAmmonia; lipaseConfusion; abdominal pain
Carbamazepine, before the first doseHLA-B*1502 in Asian ancestrySJS and TEN with the allele
Carbamazepine, duringLevel at steady state (5 days) and weeks later; CBC, basic metabolic panel, liver testsIt induces its own metabolism, so levels typically settle only at 2 to 4 weeks; marrow, sodium, liver
LamotrigineLiver tests, basic metabolic panel, CBC at baseline only; no levelsDosing follows the clinical response
Interactions
Drug, and what is addedEffect on that drug

Valproate, with carbamazepineLevel falls

Practice
  1. 27-year-old woman with bipolar II disorder, 3 weeks into lamotrigine a few itchy pink macules on her chest since yesterday no fever, blisters or mouth sores; feels well T 37.0 °C · HR 78/min → Stop lamotrigine → any rash on lamotrigine means stopping it, because a benign rash and early Stevens-Johnson syndrome cannot be told apart; continuing at the same or a lower dose is the trap
  2. 45-year-old man with bipolar I disorder on valproate for 4 months family reports 2 days of drowsiness and confusion no abdominal pain; no jaundice; no new drugs valproate level in range · AST and ALT normal → Plasma ammonia → confusion on valproate calls for an ammonia level: a valproate metabolite blocks ammonia elimination in the urea cycle; lipase is for epigastric pain, and the platelet count tracks thrombocytopenia
  3. 34-year-old woman on valproate for bipolar I disorder for 3 years a day of epigastric pain boring to the back, with vomiting one glass of wine weekly; no gallstones on ultrasound lipase 6 times the upper limit of normal → Stop valproate → valproate pancreatitis is idiosyncratic, unrelated to dose or duration, and in most cases resolves once the drug is stopped; years on a stable dose do not exclude it
  4. 31-year-old man of Asian ancestry with bipolar I disorder carbamazepine planned for mania after lithium and valproate were not tolerated no drug allergies; liver tests and CBC normal sodium 139 mEq/L → HLA-B*1502 testing → before carbamazepine in a patient of Asian ancestry, screen for HLA-B*1502 and avoid the drug if it is present, because of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis; levels come after steady state, and ammonia belongs to valproate
  5. 24-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder has a positive pregnancy test started carbamazepine 4 months ago takes a combined estrogen-progestin pill daily no missed pills, no vomiting, no other drugs → Induction of liver enzymes → carbamazepine induces cytochrome P450 enzymes, which clear the oral contraceptive faster and can end in an unplanned pregnancy; enzyme inhibition is how valproate raises lamotrigine, and protein binding matters for valproate when albumin is low
  6. 38-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder, stable on lamotrigine for a year now in a manic episode; valproate is being added no rash; liver tests, CBC and sodium normal BP 122/78 mm Hg · HR 84/min → Lower the lamotrigine dose → valproate inhibits lamotrigine clearance, raising its level and the rash risk, so the lamotrigine dose comes down and titration slows; lamotrigine levels are not needed, because dosing follows the clinical response
  7. 29-year-old man with bipolar II disorder stopped lamotrigine 3 weeks ago had taken a stable dose for a year; ran out while traveling mood now low; wants to restart; never had a rash → Restart at the starting dose and titrate up → after lamotrigine is stopped suddenly, it restarts at the initial dose with titration rather than at the old dose, since rapid dose escalation raises the rash risk; levels are not needed
  8. 52-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder, confused for 2 days carbamazepine dose raised 3 weeks ago no vomiting, diarrhea or diuretics; no rash sodium 124 mEq/L · ammonia normal · AST and ALT normal → Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone → carbamazepine carries a dose-dependent risk of SIADH and hyponatremia; hyperammonemic encephalopathy belongs to valproate, and DRESS typically brings a rash with organ involvement 2 to 8 weeks in

Transferable rule

On an anticonvulsant mood stabilizer, name the effect before the next step: a rash on lamotrigine and pancreatitis on valproate stop the drug whatever the dose, confusion on valproate calls for an ammonia, and carbamazepine needs its HLA-B*1502 screen before the first dose in Asian ancestry.
